title: Invention of the Printing Press
key_facts: Johannes Gutenberg developed movable-type printing in mid-15th century Mainz
Enabled rapid, relatively inexpensive reproduction of texts
Catalyzed spread of literacy, scholarship, and religious debate
causes: Demand for books and administrative records in growing towns and universities
Advances in metallurgy, inks, and paper availability
Cultural appetite for classical and contemporary texts
outcome: Explosion of printed materials: bibles, pamphlets, scientific works
Acceleration of Renaissance humanism and later the Reformation
Standardization of language, knowledge, and information networks
impacts: Lowered cost of knowledge dissemination and democratized access
Foundation for scientific communication and peer circulation
Shaped religious movements and state administration
